# BriefLoop

> BriefLoop is a local agent workbench for sourced briefings. Connect a CLI you already have (Codex, Opencode, Claude Code, Kimi, Hermes, DeepSeek Reasonix or MiMo Code), ask a question or request a report, and get an editable draft with an independent evaluation and reusable learning.

Current version: 0.17.1
Python: 3.11 or newer
Install: git clone https://github.com/Stahl-G/briefloop.git && cd briefloop && ./start.sh
Package: briefloop-local on PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/briefloop-local/)
Bridged CLIs need Node.js 20+ on the same machine.
Interface language: Chinese. Report body can be written in Chinese or English.

## What it does

- Workspaces: one local folder per project holds chats, sources, report versions, scores and skills.
- Sources: upload files or fetch public pages; every source keeps its original, extracted text and provenance.
- Reports: BriefLoop (the main agent) plans research, Scout collects sources inside a shared budget, Analyst drafts, and you edit the draft directly in the browser.
- Independent evaluation: Evaluator scores the draft in its own session; one automatic revision can follow, and unresolved items stay visible.
- Learning: Wiki Maintainer turns your edits and feedback into Wiki notes, Skill Proposer proposes skills, and only verified candidates are enabled.
- Templates and context: reusable Word templates keep your layout, manual sections stay empty for you to fill, and an optional company background base tracks public updates.
- Delivery: Word is produced on demand from a fixed version; a formal release can be exported with its evidence and review record.

## Runtime facts

- Codex and Opencode run through native managers; Claude Code, Kimi, Hermes, DeepSeek Reasonix and MiMo Code run through a local NDJSON bridge.
- The host CLI owns permissions and network access. Codex can enforce read-only or workspace-write sandboxes and per-turn web search; Opencode can enforce read-only through its permission rules; bridged hosts run with their own permission model.
- Turning on the chat's online switch grants the host its own web tools (for Claude Code: WebSearch and WebFetch). Whether the call succeeds is decided by that host's account and permissions.
- Model lists come from each host's catalogue, and any model ID can be typed in. "default" means the model the host itself is configured with.
- Only Codex supports mid-run steering. Research budgets are per report, shared across scouts, and never extended automatically.

## Rules for agents

- Start from a source checkout or the published package; do not invent other install paths.
- Ask the user before enabling online search, spending research budget, or producing a formal delivery.
- Read the workspace's own sources and stored versions; do not treat a model's summary as evidence.
- Keep credentials out of workspaces, reports and logs.
